entries.what_happened: One manuscript, 'A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg-Ganea conjecture' (OpenAI, dated September 23, 2026). Its Theorem thm:main asserts a finitely generated residually finite group G with integral cohomological dimension cd_Z(G) = 2 and geometric dimension gd(G) = 3, and that G has no two-dimensional classifying space, whatever the number of its cells. Construction: start from the presentation complex K of <x,y | x²=y⁵, x²=(xy⁻¹)³>, which is integrally acyclic (the exponent-sum matrix has determinant 1). Lemma geometric-seed flag-triangulates K into a finite two-dimensional flag complex L with vanishing reduced integral homology and a nontrivial homomorphism alpha from pi_1(L) to SU(2), given by an explicit pair of unit quaternions. G is the height kernel ker(lambda) in the right-angled Artin group A_L, where lambda sends each standard generator to 1 (a Bestvina-Brady group). Proposition model: G is countable, finitely generated and residually finite; G acts freely on an integrally acyclic two-dimensional level complex X with one vertex orbit and finitely many cell orbits; the cellular chains of X give an exact sequence 0 -> Λ^(D) -> Λ^(S) -> Λ -> Z -> 0 with Λ = Z[G], so cd_Z(G) ≤ 2; cd_Z(G) ≥ 2 by restriction to a Z² subgroup; and the contractible three-dimensional cubical space E, on which G acts freely, gives a three-dimensional K(G,1) = E/G, so gd(G) ≤ 3. The lower bound excluding a two-dimensional K(G,1) is by contradiction. Theorem presentation: for a residually finite group Γ with a finite list D of words trivial in Γ whose chains form a free basis of the cycle module, and any two-dimensional K(Γ,1), there is η > 0 such that every SU(2)-labelling of the generator edges within distance η of 1, with trivial product around every translate of every word in D, has trivial product around every closed edge path. Proposition small-labels: for every ε > 0 there are labels on the edges of X within ε of 1, with trivial product around every triangle, and nontrivial product around some closed edge path; these are pulled back from alpha along direction maps from X to L. Taking ε < η gives a contradiction, so gd(G) = 3.
entries.delivers: Disproves the Eilenberg-Ganea statement as the list words it, on the integral reading. The list states that a group with cohomological dimension 2 has a two-dimensional K(G,1); the manuscript states the conjecture with integral cohomological dimension (introduction) and refutes it with one group, which is enough for a universal claim. The list names no coefficient ring, and the manuscript uses only integral coefficients. The witness is countable, finitely generated, residually finite, of type FP_infinity, and has a finite free resolution of length two over Z[G]. The manuscript says it is not finitely presented, because L has nontrivial fundamental group and the Bestvina-Brady criterion applies. So the counterexample does not cover finitely presented groups. The paper's statement of the problem matches the list's on the integral reading. The introduction says the result answers the question negatively.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, nothing remains of the integral form of the bullet. Not addressed: the same question with other coefficient rings, which the list does not specify and the manuscript does not use; the question restricted to finitely presented groups, since the witness is not finitely presented; and cohomological dimensions other than 2, which the manuscript does not treat.
entries.direction: disproves the conjecture (integral cd 2, geometric dimension 3)
entries.object: G = ker(lambda) in the right-angled Artin group A_L, a height kernel of an explicit finite flag complex L obtained from the presentation complex of <x,y | x²=y⁵, x²=(xy⁻¹)³> by an explicit subdivision and cone construction. The group, its level complex X and the three-dimensional classifying space E/G are explicit. The non-existence of a two-dimensional classifying space is proved by contradiction, using compactness of arbitrary products and choice, and gives no explicit object.
entries.conditional_on: No unproven hypothesis beyond standard foundations: ZFC (choice, and Tychonoff's theorem for arbitrary products, which the comparison theorem needs for presentations of arbitrary cardinality), standard CW and covering-space theory, and finite-dimensional degree theory (Milnor). The height-kernel framework of Bestvina-Brady and Dicks-Leary is cited, but the properties used in the proof are proved in the manuscript. The Bestvina-Brady finite-presentability criterion is cited only for the remark that G is not finitely presented. Gerstenhaber-Rothaus and Froyshov are cited for the degree formula; the manuscript proves the localized statement it uses (Lemma localized-degree). No other OpenAI manuscript is used. Leary-Petrosyan (LP2026) appears only as background in the introduction.
entries.doubts: Lemma localized-degree (sections/degree.tex) is written in condensed form. The equivariant perturbation and transversality step is settled in a few sentences, including 'By compactness, sufficiently small perturbations introduce no zeros elsewhere'. The displayed argument establishes the degree only modulo an odd prime p larger than b. The Remark then states the exact value b·sign(det B) by repeating the argument for arbitrarily large primes, which the displayed proof does not spell out. The text flags no step as sketched or hedged.

entries.not_relevant_because: The manuscript disproves the Eilenberg-Ganea statement for one group and says nothing about whether connected subcomplexes of aspherical two-dimensional complexes are aspherical. Whitehead's question appears only as background in the introduction, which recalls the Bestvina-Brady dichotomy that at least one of the Eilenberg-Ganea and Whitehead conjectures fails for certain flag triangulations. The failure of Eilenberg-Ganea here is consistent with that dichotomy but does not decide the Whitehead side.
